subject: Surface-level insights: tenant widgetization & cost/latency breakouts
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@nebulahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Need finer tenant-level spend + latency tiles for exec review

Hi Rachel,

Quick one — our finance and infra teams are preparing an executive packet for next Tuesday and they asked for a concise dashboards showing per-tenant (customer) cost and 95th/99th tail latency over the last 30 days. Right now the Console aggregates at the workspace level and we can't slice down to tenant slices for our multi-tenant product.

Specifically we need: 
- Per-tenant token spend (daily) and 30-day trend
- 95th and 99th percentile tail latency per tenant, by route (chat/generation/embeddings)
- Anomalies flagged where cost increased >30% week-over-week

Are there existing APIs or quick exports we can use? If not, is there an ETA for a small dashboard widget set we could embed in our customer portal or just a CSV export we can ship to the execs?

Thanks — very tight timeline; any quick guidance is appreciated.

— Sara
Director of Platform
Nebula Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@nebulahealth.com>, Neil Jacobs <neil.jacobs@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Need finer tenant-level spend + latency tiles for exec review

Thanks Sara — looping in Marissa (CS) and Karthik (Product) to scope a rapid path. Laura I copied to flag for engineering support if we need a small spike.

Short answer: we can deliver an export + a lightweight set of Console widgets within 5–10 business days depending on backend traces and whether tenant IDs are already surfaced in our billing telemetry. 

Immediate asks from our side so we can triage today: 
1) Can you share 2–3 tenant IDs (example tenant IDs, not PII) and a short access time window you care about?
2) Do you need route-level breakdowns in the initial deliverable, or is tenant-level aggregated spend + a single aggregate latency metric acceptable for the exec packet?
3) If you have a sample CSV or an existing internal report, please attach — will speed up mapping.

Proposed quick deliverable (MVP): 
- CSV export with per-tenant daily token spend + overall p95 latency (by day)
- A one-page Console widget sketch we can iterate on for the customer portal

If that works for you I'll coordinate a quick Spike with Engineering and share a timeline by EOD.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@nebulahealth.com>, Neil Jacobs <neil.jacobs@nebulahealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T12:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Need finer tenant-level spend + latency tiles for exec review

Thanks Rachel — quick technical note and I attached two artifacts (tenant-sample.csv and dashboard-sketch.png). The sample shows the shape our billing exporter produces when tenant_id is present. Two important constraints I want to call out for the spike: 

- Current billing export surfaces workspace_id + route but tenant_id is only present when customers use token-level attribution headers. If Nebula already sends tenant_id in the X-Tenant header, mapping is trivial. If not, we'll need to backfill via logs which adds time.
- Latency percentiles: we can calculate p95/p99 from tracing events but only if tracing retention covers the 30-day window. If not, we'll provide p95/p99 on a sampled basis and mark confidence.

Attachments: 
- tenant-sample.csv (attachment stub) — columns: date, workspace_id, tenant_id, route, tokens_consumed, duration_ms
- dashboard-sketch.png (attachment stub) — rough Console mockup for a per-tenant card (spend sparkline, p95/p99 bar, anomaly flag)

Ask for Product/Engineering: can we approve a timeboxed spike (2 dev days + 1 infra half-day) to validate telemetry mapping and produce the CSV export? If approved I can own the CS side and validate with Nebula.

— Marissa
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara@nebulahealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Need finer tenant-level spend + latency tiles for exec review

Thanks team — marking this high priority. 

Decision and next steps: 
- Approve a 2-working-day engineering spike to validate tenant_id mapping and generate a CSV export.
- If tenant_id is not present in their traffic headers, we will do a targeted log-join backfill (estimate +3 business days).
- Karthik will own product acceptance criteria for the widget (binary: show per-tenant daily spend + p95/p99 for requested routes). Marissa will validate outputs against Nebula.
- Rachel please ask Nebula to share 2 sample tenant IDs and confirm whether they send X-Tenant headers; Marissa will validate the attached sample.

I'll block a pair of dev hours tomorrow morning (engineer: Diego Fernandez) to kick off the spike and we should have an export ready for review by EOD Thursday if mapping is straightforward. If not, we'll escalate and share an updated ETA by Friday.

Laura Bennett
Engineering Manager — Observability & Instrumentation
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
